messages.content:
You are an experienced UK building control surveyor. Answer the question about the work item
in the JSON state. Choose exactly one label:
- not_notifiable: No Building Regulations notice needed: not building work (reg 3), only Schedule 4 work, or an exempt building (reg 9, Schedule 2).
- competent_person_scheme: Notifiable work listed in Schedule 3: a registered competent person can self-certify it (reg 12(6)(a)); otherwise a building notice is needed.
- building_notice_or_full_plans: Building work not covered by Schedules 3 or 4: a building notice or a full plans application to building control (reg 12(2)).
- full_plans_required: Building work that must have a full plans application: the Fire Safety Order applies to the building (reg 12(3)), it fronts a private street (12(4)), or H4 applies (building over or near a sewer, 12(5)).
Reply with JSON only: {"label": "<one label>", "probabilities": {"<label>": <0..1>, ...}} with a
probability for every label, summing to 1.

Under the Building Regulations 2010 in England, which notification route applies to this work item if it is carried out on its own in the building described?

{"work_item": "Replace existing rooflight with new unit in same opening", "project": "House in England", "jurisdiction": "England. The Building Regulations 2010 as amended.", "clauses": [{"ref": "Sch 3 para 10", "document": "BR2010", "text": "10. Installation, as a replacement, of a window, rooflight, roof window or door in an existing dwelling. | A person registered in respect of that type of work by Assure Certification Limited, ... ... Blue Flame Certification Limited, CERTASS Limited, Certsure LLP, by Fensa Limited under the Fenestration Self-Assessment Scheme or by NAPIT Registration Limited ..., ...."}, {"ref": "para 10.6", "document": "ADL1-2021", "text": "10.6 The term controlled fitting refers to the entire unit of a window, roof window, rooflight or door, including the frame. Replacing glazing, or a window or door in its existing frame is not providing a controlled fitting. Such work does not need to meet the energy efficiency requirements. Extension of a dwelling"}, {"ref": "para 10.1", "document": "ADL1-2021", "text": "10.1 This section provides guidance for new elements in existing dwellings, including all the following types of work. a. Providing a new thermal element in an existing dwelling – follow paragraph 10.1. b. Providing a replacement thermal element in an existing dwelling – follow paragraph 10.2. c. Replacing windows, doors or rooflights (controlled fittings) in an existing dwelling – follow paragraphs 10.3 to 10.6. d. Extending an existing dwelling – follow paragraphs 10.7 to 10.11. e. Adding a conservatory or porch to an existing dwelling – follow paragraphs 10.12 and 10.13. NOTE: Guidance for renovating elements in existing dwellings is given in Section 11. New and replacement fabric elements"}]}

message.content:
Replacing the whole rooflight unit in an existing dwelling is providing a controlled fitting, so this is building work. Schedule 3 paragraph 10 expressly lists replacement windows, rooflights, roof windows and doors in an existing dwelling as work that a registered installer (e.g. FENSA, CERTASS or Certsure) can self-certify. Without such an installer, a building notice would be needed.

Some residual uncertainty remains: if only the glazing were replaced within the existing frame, ADL1 paragraph 10.6 says it would not be a controlled fitting and would not be notifiable. Here the description says "new unit", so it is a full replacement.

message.reasoning: Replacing a whole rooflight unit falls under Schedule 3, paragraph 10 as a competent person scheme matter, since a whole unit replacement counts as a "new unit" rather than mere glazing replacement, which wouldn't be a controlled fitting.
